# Turn your phone into a pocket analyst with Genie One

**Hook:**
Imagine having a mini business analyst in your pocket. With the Genie One mobile app, you can ask questions about your sales reports, customer emails, or meeting notes and get clear, data-driven answers—anywhere, anytime. No spreadsheets, no waiting for reports. This guide shows you how to set it up in minutes.

## Before you start
- A **free Genie One account** (sign up at genie.one).
- The **Genie One mobile app** installed on your phone (iOS or Android).
- A **spreadsheet, email thread, or note** you want to analyse (CSV, XLSX, or plain text).
- Roughly **10 minutes** of your time.

---

## Step 1 — Open the Genie One app and sign in
Open the Genie One app on your phone. You’ll see the login screen. Tap **Sign in** and enter the email and password you used to create your account. If you don’t have an account yet, tap **Create account** and follow the prompts.

💬 Example:
```
Email: your.name@company.com
Password: ••••••••
```

You'll know it worked when you see your name or profile picture in the top-right corner of the screen.

---

## Step 2 — Tap the “+” icon to upload your file
On the main screen, look for a big **“+”** button in the bottom-right corner. Tap it. A menu will pop up with options like **Upload file**, **Connect cloud**, or **Paste text**. Choose **Upload file**.

💬 Example:
```
Tap “Upload file” → select “Sales_Report_Q2.xlsx” from your Downloads folder
```

You'll know it worked when you see a green checkmark and the file name at the top of the screen.

---

## Step 3 — Ask your first question about the data
After the file uploads, you’ll see a chat box at the bottom of the screen. Type your question in plain English. For example:
💬 Example:
```
"Which product had the highest sales in May?"
```

You'll know it worked when the app starts typing a response in the chat window within a few seconds.

---

## Step 4 — Read the insight and ask a follow-up
The app will show a clear answer like:
> “Product X had the highest sales in May with $18,450.”

If the answer isn’t quite right, tap the message and say:
💬 Example:
```
"Show me the breakdown by region for Product X in May."
```

You'll know it worked when the app updates the answer with a new chart or table.

---

## Step 5 — Save the conversation for later
To keep your insights handy, tap the **bookmark icon** (looks like a ribbon) next to your question in the chat. The conversation will appear in your **Saved** tab for quick access next time.

💬 Example:
```
Tap the ribbon icon → choose “Save this thread”
```

You'll know it worked when you see a confirmation message: “Saved to your library.”

---

## Step 6 — Share the insight with your team
To send the result to a colleague, tap the **share icon** (an arrow pointing up from a box) next to the answer. Choose **Copy link** or **Send via email**. The link opens the full chat in their browser.

💬 Example:
```
Tap the share icon → choose “Copy link” → paste into Slack
```

You'll know it worked when your colleague confirms they can open the link and see the same chart.

---

## Common mistakes
- **Mistake:** Typing a question that’s too vague.
  **Fix:** Be specific. Instead of “Tell me about sales,” say “Which product had the highest sales in May?”

- **Mistake:** Uploading a locked or password-protected file.
  **Fix:** Save the file as a normal XLSX or CSV first, then upload.

- **Mistake:** Expecting the app to send emails or update databases automatically.
  **Fix:** Genie One can draft insights, but it can’t send emails or change your CRM directly.

---

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life:** Got a messy spreadsheet from your kid’s school fundraiser? Upload it and ask, “How much did each class raise?” in seconds.
- **For your business or work:** Stuck in a meeting with a client report you haven’t read? Paste the key numbers into Genie One and ask, “What are the top 3 risks in this quarter’s data?” before the call starts.
- **If you're just getting started:** Start with a small file—like a CSV of your last month’s expenses—and ask one simple question. You’ll see how fast it turns numbers into clear answers.

---

## Try it now
Open the Genie One app, upload a small file (like a CSV or XLSX), and ask:
💬 Example:
```
"What are the top 3 expenses in this file?"
```
See how it turns your data into a clear list—right on your phone.
